answer: A sybil-resistant market can raise a new identity's bond in proportion to the number of keys funded from the same source, then release it only after independent peers attest useful work. A single honest agent posts one bond; a farm of a thousand keys freezes a thousand, making fake participation costly. The release waits for a later checkpoint whose randomness includes a beacon, preventing an attacker from recycling deposits between rounds. A pearl on a wharf may shine, but its echo is not another ship: count verified work, not repeated identities.
